name: Ichechuku Enwuka
missingPieces: D1 omits the hardcoded JWT secret finding (sankofa-legacy-admin-2019). D2 chain skips the stored XSS (02:18:47) and open redirect (02:21:13) hops. D4 does not answer the colleague-evidence prompt and cites no NDPA section number.
feedback: D1 is the strongest part of this submission. You catalogued nine of the ten findings with a real evidence line for each, the SQLi payload admin' OR '1'='1 at 02:15:31, the MD5 source line, the alg:none Token2, the 185.220.101.9 XSS beacon at 02:18:47, the XXE ENTITY SYSTEM file:///etc/passwd, the path traversal at 02:24:02, the open redirect at 02:21:13, and the cookie flags. You also nailed the decoy, naming the custom HS256 checker and proving it safe at the mechanism level because hash_equals is constant time, while correctly keeping alg:none as a real bug elsewhere, which is exactly the verdict the key wants. What cost you here was the missing hardcoded JWT secret finding and a few OWASP slips, alg:none and the missing expiry are A07 not A01, but since proof beats label and CWE-328 for MD5 is a defensible variant I credited those. D2 has good bones, you reconciled SQLi, the 312 row PII pull, and the XXE-then-path-traversal escalation to capture lines, and your CVSS vectors are full strings with justification rather than bare numbers, which earns real credit. Two things held it back, the chain dropped the stored XSS and open redirect hops so it reads as three stages instead of the full progression, and your SQLi and JWT vectors use A:H when the auth bypass does not touch availability, so the correct vector is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1 rather than 9.8. Your impact section was good, 312 customers and roughly 4,000,000 NGN extrapolated from a stated 20 row sample tied to the BoltCash launch in six weeks, with the assumption named. D3 is solid, the exec summary lands on customers and naira, the threat model names The Griot over Tor, the decoy is disproved correctly, and crucially your remediation table is ordered by effort not severity, delete the alg:none override in under an hour first, then parameterise the login query, then the hashing migration last because it is weeks of work, which is the right axis. Your two detection stopgaps are concrete, the WAF regex on login.php POST for boolean tautologies and the SIEM rule decoding the legacy_admin_jwt header for alg:none, both with false positive rates. The report body only substantiates four findings though, so it under-represents the full catalogue you found in D1. D4 answers three of the four prompts in your own voice, the journalist refusal, the written report to Amaka Eze, and the resign-rather-than-cover-up line, and you cite ISC2 Canon 1 and 2 by number, but you skipped the colleague-with-evidence prompt entirely and you named only the 72 hour rule without the NDPA 2023 section, which is section 40 for the NDPC notification within 72 hours and section 41 for notifying the 312 data subjects on high risk. The single most important fix is to defend your CVSS vectors metric by metric, an auth bypass is A:N not A:H, because a wrong availability value undermines the prioritisation the whole report rests on.
